featured.reason: Addy Osmani's Agent Skills (MIT): 25 SKILL.md engineering workflows (spec-driven development, planning, TDD, code review, debugging, security hardening, browser testing via Chrome DevTools MCP, shipping) plus 9 lifecycle slash commands (/spec, /plan, /build, /test, /review, /ship...), 4 reviewer personas and shared checklists. Directly installable process discipline for coding agents.
ideas: Install it in Codex with `codex plugin marketplace add addyosmani/agent-skills` and `codex plugin add agent-skills@agent-skills`, then run `@spec-driven-development` before your next ai-daily-radar change so the agent writes a spec and task plan before touching code.

Pair skills/browser-testing-with-devtools with the Chrome DevTools MCP to have Claude Code check the live dashboard after each deploy: console errors, layout shifts and whether the animated background renders on a mobile-sized viewport.
Use the /webperf command and references/performance-checklist.md to audit the site's Core Web Vitals on mobile, then turn the findings into small, test-backed commits with /build.

Study evals/ (structural checks, TF-IDF trigger routing, behavioral expectations[]) and copy the pattern to test your own shared skills, such as CLI-Anything or MoneyPrinterTurbo, so agents pick the right skill for the right prompt.

Read docs/skill-anatomy.md and the .claude-plugin / .codex-plugin manifests, then package one of your Android or iOS build routines as a cross-agent plugin that installs the same way in Claude Code and Codex.

news_highlights.title: Show HN: Get your coding agent off ~2019 JavaScript, onto modern web primitives
news_highlights.why_it_matters: Chrome, Edge, Firefox and MDN now ship a skill that feeds coding agents vetted guides for 250 modern web features, searched offline with no API keys. It installs in Claude Code and Codex, and its legacy-scan command can flag old patterns in an existing site.

news_highlights.title: Git security vulnerabilities announced
news_highlights.why_it_matters: Git 2.56.1 fixes six bugs, including code execution during a recursive clone of a malicious repo. Any agent or script that clones untrusted repos with submodules should update Git now or avoid recursive clones until it does.

news_highlights.title: AlphaProof Code
news_highlights.why_it_matters: DeepMind agents wrote over six million lines of Lean to prove security properties of Signal's actual protocol code in four weeks, with humans reviewing about 1%. It shows a practical pattern: humans write the spec, agents do the proofs, and a checker verifies them.

news_highlights.title: After 7 months, Glasswing overwelms maintainers with underwhelming findings
news_highlights.why_it_matters: VulnCheck counts 37,966 AI-reported findings but only 217 fixes, and curl rejected 19 of its first 34 scanner reports. AI bug reports still need human triage, so budget for that before pointing a scanner at your own projects.

news_highlights.title: AI usage generates a fragile codebase
news_highlights.why_it_matters: An engineer who writes nearly all his code with AI lists the costs he sees: shallow tests, over-complex helpers, and reviews too rushed to keep up. It's a useful checklist for reviewing what your coding agents ship.
